citeinfo.title: Chesapeake Bay River Input Monitoring Network 1985-2023: Annual loads

descript.abstract: Nitrogen, phosphorus, and suspended-sediment loads, and changes in loads, in major rivers across the Chesapeake Bay watershed have been calculated using monitoring data from the Chesapeake Bay River Input Monitoring (RIM) Network stations for the period 1985 through 2023. Nutrient and suspended-sediment loads and changes in loads were determined by applying a weighted regression approach called WRTDS (Weighted Regression on Time, Discharge, and Season). The load results represent the total mass of nitrogen, phosphorus, and suspended sediment that was exported from each of the RIM watersheds.
descript.purpose: The purpose of this dataset is to communicate the annual loads of nitrogen, phosphorus, and suspended sediment being transported by the nontidal portion of the major rivers in the Bay watershed.

procstep.procdesc:
Methods: KConc (Kalman concentration) and KLoad (Kalman load/flux) were computed using the residual errors gained from the daily WRTDS with Kalman filtering (WRTDS-K) models from days with an observed sample concentration at each RIM monitoring location. The model residuals are standardized, for each observed sample day, and are then simulated via Monte Carlo resamplings for the nonoverlapping gap interval days (before and after the days with observed sample measurements) with a lag-1 auto-correlation regression. Unlike regular WRTDS, WRTDS-K stores the true sampled measurements as part of its estimation output.
FNConc (flow-normalized concentration) and FNLoad (flow-normalized load/flux) were computed by estimating an expected concentration for each day of the record by using the observed daily discharge for that day. Each day in the record (for example January 1, 1985, January 1, 1986... January 1, 2022) is binned into a three dimensional matrix of regression results and the estimate for that day is determined using linear interpolation of all the results stored in the matrix. By using each site's entire history of discharge, the loads are normalized to remove year-to-year variability from input sources or management practices. WRTDS stores a modeled measurement for every day as part of its estimation output (no sampled measurement values are retained like with WRTDS-K).
The application of WRTDS-K to generate the loads provided in this table is documented in Zhang and Hirsch (2019). The application of WRTDS to generate the flow-normalized loads provided in this table is documented in Hirsch and others (2010) and in Chanat and others (2016). WRTDS and WRTDS-K are available in the R (version 4.3.1) software package EGRET - Exploration and Graphics for RivEr Trends (version 3.0.9; Hirsch and DeCicco, 2015).
USGS station and parameter code information can be viewed at waterdata.usgs.gov/nwis and nwis.waterdata.usgs.gov/usa/nwis/pmcodes, respectively.
